objects.label: Guitar string
objects.detect_hint: a guitar, ukulele or any plucked string instrument, or a close-up of strings and frets
objects.concept: Standing waves: a shorter string vibrates faster, so the note is higher
objects.answer: A shorter string vibrates faster, so the note is higher.

chapters.title: Standing waves
captions: Pressing a fret shortens the string. Half the length gives double the frequency: f = v / 2L.
A string also vibrates in whole-number patterns: harmonics n = 1, 2, 3 at f, 2f, 3f.
Wave speed depends on tension T and mass per length: f = (1/2L) sqrt(T/mu). Tighter = higher.

objects.label: Thrown ball
objects.detect_hint: any ball (tennis, football, basketball, bouncy ball, crumpled paper ball) held, thrown or bouncing
objects.concept: Projectile motion and bounce: gravity bends the path into a parabola; each bounce keeps only part of the energy
objects.answer: Gravity bends the path into a curve.

chapters.title: Projectile motion
captions: Gravity pulls the ball down all the time, so its path curves into a parabola.
Sideways speed never changes. Only the up-and-down speed does, because gravity acts down.
Air drag slows the ball, so the best angle drops below 45 degrees. Grey = no air.

chapters.title: Bounce
chapters.lead: Each bounce keeps only part of the energy.
chapters.hint: Left/right: ball type. Up/down: drop height.
captions: Each bounce is lower because the ball keeps only part of its energy: the height ratio is e squared.
Falling turns height energy into movement; the squash stores it like a spring; some is lost as heat and sound every bounce.
Bounciness depends on the material: a super ball springs back almost fully, clay absorbs the energy as heat and barely bounces.

objects.label: Bike gears
objects.detect_hint: a bicycle, its chain, chainring, cassette or rear gears
objects.concept: Gear ratio: a big front and small back gear trades pedalling force for speed
objects.answer: A big front gear and small back gear trade force for speed.

chapters.title: Gear ratio
captions: The chain links two gears. Gear ratio = front teeth / rear teeth.
Each pedal turn pulls the chain by the front teeth count, so the wheel turns by the ratio.
Energy is conserved: a higher ratio gives more speed per pedal turn but less push at the wheel.

objects.label: Boiling kettle
objects.detect_hint: a kettle, pot of water, or a cup or mug of hot drink
objects.concept: Convection: hot water rises, cool water sinks, bubbles are water turning to vapour
objects.answer: Hot water rises, cool water sinks, bubbles are vapour.

chapters.title: Convection and boiling
captions: Heated water expands and gets lighter, so it rises in the middle and sinks at the sides.
Hot spots at the bottom let vapour bubbles form (nucleation), then they rise and burst.
At 100 C extra energy goes into turning water to vapour, not heating it. That is latent heat.

objects.label: Swinging keys
objects.detect_hint: keys on a lanyard or string, a necklace, a yo-yo, anything hanging that can swing
objects.concept: Pendulum: the swing time depends on the length, not the weight
objects.answer: Swing time depends on length, not weight.

chapters.title: Swing time
captions: One swing takes T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g). A longer string swings more slowly.
The angle follows a smooth sine wave. Four times the length gives double the period.
Mass cancels out: two bobs of different mass on equal strings swing together.

objects.label: Smartphone
objects.detect_hint: a smartphone or tablet, front or back, in a hand or on a table
objects.concept: Layers: glass, touch sensor, OLED pixels, battery and logic board stacked in a few millimetres
objects.answer: About nine thin layers: glass, touch, pixels, chips and a battery.

chapters.title: Layers
captions: A phone is a sandwich of about nine thin layers, all packed into less than a centimetre.
The touch sensor is a grid of electrodes. Your finger changes the electric field, or capacitance, where you touch.
Millions of OLED pixels each make their own light. A black pixel is simply off, which saves power on dark screens.
The logic board holds processor, memory and radio chips. The processor does billions of simple steps per second.
Lithium ions move between two electrode layers as you charge and use the phone. The battery is the largest part inside.
The coil charges without a cable by magnetic induction. The camera stacks several lenses onto a tiny sensor.
